title: SINAI at eRisk@CLEF 2025: Transformer-Based and Conversational Strategies for Depression Detection
extended_summary:
This paper is not the targeted education study on AI-assisted writing feedback for secondary students. Instead, it is a CLEF 2025 shared-task notebook describing the SINAI-UJA team’s participation in eRisk@CLEF 2025 on depression detection from online conversations and LLM-based simulated dialogues. The paper addresses two problems: early detection of depression from contextualized Reddit-style discussions, and conversational depression detection through interaction with LLM-powered personas.

For Task 2, the authors developed transformer-based models using RoBERTa, MentalRoBERTa, and MentalLongformer variants. Because the organizer-provided training data lacked conversational context, they scraped additional Reddit data from /depression and /AdviceForTeens and merged this with sampled organizer data. They designed a preprocessing pipeline to structure posts and comments into target-versus-context message sequences and trained models to make early depression predictions over conversations. For the pilot task, they built a two-LLM architecture using Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct: one model acted as a conversational agent and the other as an evaluation agent estimating 21 BDI-II depressive symptoms over multiple turns.

The study population and context are online social-media users and simulated LLM personas, not students, teachers, or schools. The empirical setting is an online shared-task evaluation environment using Reddit-derived data and benchmark conversations provided through the eRisk@CLEF 2025 competition. No educational intervention, writing instruction, or secondary-school implementation is reported.

The main conclusions are that the team’s transformer pipeline for contextualized early depression detection achieved modest decision performance but strong early-ranking behavior and fast inference, highlighting a trade-off between timeliness and precision. In the pilot conversational task, their structured dual-LLM approach performed best overall among participating teams, suggesting that modular conversational design can support efficient symptom elicitation in constrained mental-health assessment scenarios. As evidence-based resolution for the retrieval query, this paper is a false positive and not a variant of the sought 2025 study titled "The role of AI assisted writing feedback in developing secondary students writing skills."
quality_tier_rationale: The provided paper is not the targeted education study and does not evaluate an AI or technology intervention in a K-12 educational context. It is a CLEF shared-task system paper on depression detection and conversational assessment, with benchmark results but no education-relevant study design, learner sample, or academic outcomes aligned to the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention or student learning impact is studied in this paper. Reported metrics concern depression-detection task performance (e.g., F1, DCHR, ADODL, ASHR) rather than educational outcomes, so impact for the education KG is not applicable.
